rail_guard.text: Hull Paragon. End of the line, and proud of it. The trains to London are Hull Trains, the city's own, running to King's Cross since 2000.
All aboard! Trains go to any station you've been to. Mind the gap and the gulls.

hul_fern.text: Nah then! You'll want a fern? A fern. The cream box, there. Hull's got its own fern company, always has. Red boxes? Never seen one till I went to Leeds.
Hull's a funny old place. We say 'tenfoot' for the back alley between the terraces, 'nanna' for nan, and 'duck' when we like you.

hul_bobber.text: I was a bobber on the fish dock: we unloaded the catch before dawn, swinging the baskets up out of the hold. Hessle Road never slept.
Hull had over 300 trawlers once. Three weeks at sea, three days at home, and you spent the three days on Hessle Road in your best suit.

hul_culture.text: I was a volunteer in 2017. Blue coat, big smile. We had Blade in the square, ten thousand people on the waterfront and a nude photo shoot painted blue. It was a year, all right.
Hull stopped apologising for itself that year. Hasn't started again since.

hul_ferryman.text: The big ferries sail overnight from King George Dock to Rotterdam. You go to bed in Hull and wake up in Holland, which is a good trick.
Hull's always faced the other way: east, over the North Sea. More Dutch in our history than Yorkshire likes to admit.

hul_patty_fan.text: Patty and chips, love. A patty's mashed potato and sage, battered and deep-fried. Pattie butty if you put it in a bread cake. You'll not get one west of Goole.
Don't call it a fishcake. There's no fish in it. That's the point.
